worktree's `.git` pointer — is refused as well. `.git` is inside the project root
but is not project content, and no instruction file belongs there; writing a
managed block into `config` or a hook would corrupt the repository rather than
configure an agent. The git directory is recognised by its structure rather than
by its name, so a repository whose administrative directory is not called `.git`
— `git init --separate-git-dir=admin`, or a checkout driven by `GIT_DIR` — is
covered by the same refusal.

The landing must also be an agent-instruction file. An alias exists so that
`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` can share one instruction file, so a target that is
markdown by extension, or a rules file such as `.cursorrules`, is written; a
target that is some other existing file — a `Makefile`, `.envrc`, or
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — is refused rather than having a managed block
appended to it. A target that does not exist yet is still created, which is what
the dangling-alias case below relies on, and a target this command wrote on an
earlier run stays writable whatever it is named. Hard links are supported only
between `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, which may share one inode and are updated
once. The generated `.entire/graph-agent.md` guide must remain a distinct file.
A managed target whose inode carries any other name is refused before anything
is written, because an inode's other names cannot be read back from the file —
`ln .git/config CLAUDE.md` resolves to `CLAUDE.md`, spells no `.git` component and looks like an
ordinary regular file — so a second name that reaches `config`, a hook or a
build file cannot be told from a harmless one. Share an instruction file through
a symlink instead. A directory, named pipe,
socket, device, or other non-regular target is rejected with its type named in
the error. A dangling alias between `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` is supported;
the shared target is created and updated once.

A relative symlink target may not step above the project root and later
re-enter it through another alias. On Windows, a UNC target whose share cannot
be matched to the repository's own UNC spelling is refused before it is probed;
this means a mapped-drive checkout must use that mapped-drive spelling rather
than an UNC spelling of the same directory. A Windows reparse target is also
refused when its authoritative NT spelling cannot be represented without
changing meaning in the confined relative operation. This includes raw
alternate separators, absolute NT dot components, trailing dots or spaces, and
non-DOS device namespaces; an informational extended-path display name alone
does not change the target Windows resolves.

Each distinct file must contain either no Entire Graph marker tokens or exactly
one begin marker followed by one end marker. Marker tokens in examples, code
fences, or comments still count because they make the replacement range
ambiguous.

If either path or marker layout fails preflight, the command stops before
creating or changing `.entire/graph-agent.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `CLAUDE.md`.
After preflight succeeds, a rerun:

- regenerates `.entire/graph-agent.md`;
- appends a block to an unmanaged instruction file;
- replaces one valid managed block in place;
- preserves all content outside the managed block; and
- produces byte-identical files when no inputs have changed.

### Recovering from invalid instruction files

The error names the file and the condition that blocked the run. To recover:

1. Back up `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
2. Replace any directory or other non-regular target with a regular file, or
   move it aside if the instruction file should be created.
3. In each regular file, keep either zero Entire Graph marker tokens or exactly
   one complete begin/end pair in that order. Reword marker strings shown in
   examples or comments.
4. Preserve user-owned text outside the intended managed block.
5. Rerun `entire graph init-agents --repo .` and confirm that each independent
   instruction file contains one managed block.

## Removal

There is no removal command. To deactivate, delete
`.entire/graph-agent.md` and remove the managed block, including both marker
lines, from `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. Delete `.entire/` or either instruction
file only if it is otherwise empty.

## Working-tree queries bypass the cache

The interactive query family reads the working tree by default and rebuilds its
snapshot on every query, whether or not the activation files are committed. Use
`--head` when committed-tree semantics are acceptable and cache reuse matters.
See the [operations cache guide](operations.md#working-tree-queries).

## Client notes

### Claude Code

Claude Code loads the repository's `CLAUDE.md` at session start and resolves
live `@` imports. The managed direct pointer loads `.entire/graph-agent.md`.
When `CLAUDE.md` already imports `AGENTS.md`, the inheritance layout avoids a
second direct guide pointer.

A session opened before activation does not see the new files. Start a fresh
session or task in the repository after running `init-agents`.

### Other clients

Clients that read a root `AGENTS.md` encounter the direct pointer text. Clients
that do not resolve `@` imports must follow the written instruction and read
`.entire/graph-agent.md` themselves. Whether they do so depends on the client
and model, so verify the behavior rather than assuming it.

## Verifying the activation chain

Each layer has an observable check:

1. **Installation.** `entire version` and `entire graph version` both succeed;
   the second prints the installed release, such as `v0.4.0`.
2. **Files.** The three managed paths exist. Each independent instruction file
   has exactly one ordered marker pair, and
   `diff <(entire graph agent-guide) .entire/graph-agent.md` is empty. If
   `CLAUDE.md` imports `AGENTS.md`, confirm its managed block contains the
   inheritance notice rather than another direct guide import.
3. **Instruction load.** Start a fresh agent session and give it a
   code-location task. The client-side signal depends on the client; behavior
   is checked in the next step.
4. **Adoption.** The session's first code-locating tool call is
   `entire graph search ...`, before broad grep, find, or whole-file reading. If
   the agent starts elsewhere, the guide may not have loaded or may not have
   been followed. Check the activation files and the client's instruction view.
5. **Grounding.** The answer cites files and lines opened after the graph query,
   and any proposed change is checked against focused source or a narrow test.

# Revised resumption plan — bounded P1 stability sampling

User-directed on 2026-09-07. This changes sequencing and adds an explicit
approval boundary. The user subsequently resumed the revised controlled sequence, including
 diagnostics and fixes, then explicitly paused all work on 2026-09-08. The
campaign is not currently running and release gates remain unchanged. It
supersedes earlier handoff/ledger suggestions that a canary pass can lead
directly to the full campaign. Historical protocols/results remain unchanged.
The full P1 campaign still requires explicit user approval and is NOT yet
authorized.

## 0. Mandatory model routing

Every substantive step is delegated to a cheaper-model worker: routine work to
Luna and complex work to Sol. This includes implementation, diagnosis,
source/data inspection, fixture and harness work, execution/testing, result
summaries, documentation, and Git, VM, or automation/control-plane execution.
The main Astra agent only decomposes and assigns work, coordinates workers,
reviews evidence and diffs, adjudicates results, chooses the next step, and
communicates with the user. Do not create Astra subagents or silently fall
back to Astra execution; if the required cheaper worker is unavailable, report
the worker unavailable and leave the step unexecuted.

Workers may execute otherwise authorized commands or VM tasks, but delegation
adds no budget or authorization. The shared 100-run batch cap, first-issue
stops, and explicit user approval before any full campaign remain in force.
The bounded immutable repository verification authorized after the user’s
resume is complete. The active implementation worktree is
`<REPO_ROOT>`, branch `codex/graph-advantage`,
tip `ef1df4ed`. Eight controlled product invocations have been consumed and
zero clean stability batches have run. The latest immutable full-check and
compiler-correctness evidence is at source `effa358f`; the latest diagnostic
timed out. One completion diagnostic without an arbitrary elapsed product
deadline is user-authorized in principle, but execution is paused until the
user resumes and the 14 GiB/`TasksMax=512` controls are implemented and
verified. Full-campaign approval remains absent.

## 1. Resolve known issues before sampling

Close the fixture-packaging immutable-check issue; retain its failed-state
evidence. Collect/review complete partial diagnostics and investigate the
outstanding snapshot timeouts with targeted reproductions. Fix concrete
problems and run affected correctness checks. Do not launch the complete
scenario matrix to rediscover known failures or regenerate unrelated evidence.
Required repository checks still apply when relevant source changes require
them; sampling is not a substitute for correctness.

## 2. Implement a hard batch budget before any sampled run

One batch permits at most100 product/evaluator invocations TOTAL across all
workers. A run is one request, not a Go unit test. OFF and ON each consume a
run, so100 permits at most50 comparisons. Cache-warming and other preparatory
product invocations also consume the same budget; incomplete pairs must never
be silently scored. Reserve the full known cost of a pair and its preparation
before dispatch. Metadata/priming/control overhead is separately logged and
bounded, never disguised as free product work.

The launcher must receive only the selected batch manifest, not the entire
17,280-request queue with an intention to interrupt it later. It must refuse
budget overflow and duplicate dispatch across workers. Keep existing resource,
lease and process-group limits. No next batch starts until its predecessor
has been collected and reviewed. Batch counters must count attempts, including
failures and interrupted requests, without an automatic retry budget.

These hard100-run and full-approval execution controls are PLANNED, not yet
implemented by this document. Existing scripts must not be launched unchanged
as though they enforce these new boundaries. Add bounded synthetic controller
tests before use; no real corpus campaign is needed to test accounting.

## 3. Sample deliberately, then inspect each batch

Freeze the selected request list, seed/order, source/binary/configuration and
input identities before each batch. Keep the original six repositories and
workload definitions; rotate samples rather than repeatedly choosing easy
passing cells. The first batch emphasizes historical timeout/partial/mismatch
cases. Across subsequent batches cover all three profiles, both verbs, all
six repositories and each mutation scenario, with fresh OFF/ON pairs and
alternating order where applicable. Explicitly distinguish marginal coverage
from full Cartesian coverage; sampling does not exercise every combination.
Retain the original parse-dominated membership and numerical thresholds.

Stop the whole batch at the FIRST timeout, process/control failure, novel or
unreviewed partial, semantic discrepancy, source drift, missing artifact or
measurement, lease expiry, or resource-limit violation. Retain the failure
and mark unscheduled requests unrun. Do not finish100 for the sake of a round
number. Diagnose/fix first, reproduce narrowly, then prepare a new identified
batch; never automatically replay a failed one.

Known partials remain visible as partial coverage. They are not automatically
acceptable because their codes were seen before. Their complete membership
and source-grounded classification must meet the separately adopted protocol.
ADR0049 remains proposed; this plan does not silently adopt it or relabel a
failure as success. Performance warning screens retain their existing meaning
and trigger diagnosis without being presented as statistical conclusions.

## 4. Stability decision, not a benchmark result

Initial target: three consecutive clean batches, each within100 runs, on one
unchanged product/harness/protocol configuration, with the coverage described
above. A relevant fix resets the clean-batch streak; old evidence remains.
Clean means no unexpected failures, unreviewed partials, identity/semantic
mismatches, missing measurements or worker-control issues; reviewed partial
coverage counts are reported separately. Resource behavior must remain within
bounds with any warning or unexpected drift explained.

After every batch report attempted/completed/paired/unrun counts, failure and
partial counts, new issue categories, coverage, elapsed time/resource use,
what changed and the reason for the next batch. Use deterministic summaries;
do not spend model turns reviewing thousands of repetitive rows.

Three clean batches are an engineering admission threshold, not a statistical
failure-rate bound or proof of performance. Repository/request dependence
precludes treating them as independent Bernoulli trials. If coverage or
stability remains insufficient after that checkpoint, identify the concrete
gap and justify the next100-run batch; do not queue open-ended sampling or
expand to the full matrix merely because several batches ran.

## 5. Full campaign requires the user's explicit approval

Once sampling supports stability, STOP and present the evidence, remaining
risks, exact full-run manifest/request count, expected runtime and resource/cost
estimate with its assumptions, and all active stopgaps. Ask for approval then.
No full-run approval has been granted. A clean canary, three clean batches,
prior broad autonomy, heartbeat instruction or existing goal is not approval.

Before implementing any full-launch path, require an explicit approval record
bound to the proposed source/binary, harness/protocol, corpus/workload manifest
and budget. Missing or mismatched approval refuses launch. Approval must come
from the user, not a generated record or inferred consent. Material scope or
configuration changes require renewed approval. First-issue stopping applies
throughout an approved full campaign as well.

Sampled diagnostic rows remain separate from formal release measurements;
do not silently pool selected or failure-conditioned samples into the final
benchmark dataset. Failed gates and experimental defaults remain unchanged.

## Pause and handoff

Planning documents and the bounded verification status were reconciled after
the explicit resume. Work is now paused at the user’s request; do not execute,
resume or heartbeat until the user resumes. The prepared completion-diagnostic
package is WIP and has not been behaviorally validated or launched; its README
records the static checks performed. Preserve its
exact source, binary, input and control identities, plus pending test contracts;
do not alter protected untracked files. The partial package is tracked with this handoff; another instance can fetch
`https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph.git`, check out
`codex/graph-advantage`, and read this plan plus the handoff before waiting for
user resume. This resumption plan governs the earlier shutdown handoff and the
authorized but paused completion diagnostic.

"}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a bounded completion package from explicit local inputs.

This helper is deliberately offline.  It validates every source/build/input
binding before writing a new package, and defaults to a no-write dry run.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import copy
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import io
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import shutil
import stat
import tarfile
import tempfile
from typing import Any


PACKAGE_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TEMPLATE_ROOT = PACKAGE_ROOT
HASH_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
COMMIT_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,95}$")
CAP = 100
CONTROL_MEMBERS = (
    "collector/run_remote.py",
    "collector/batch_budget.py",
    "collector/campaign_gate.py",
    "collector/cloud.py",
    "collector/observe_remote.py",
    "corpus/p1_scenario.py",
    "corpus/corpus-manifest.json",
    "build-manifest.json",
    "batch-manifest.json",
    "full-check-gate.json",
    "control-hashes.txt",
)
TEMPLATE_MEMBERS = (
    "controller/controller.py",
    "collector/run_remote.py",
    "collector/batch_budget.py",
    "collector/campaign_gate.py",
    "collector/cloud.py",
    "collector/observe_remote.py",
    "corpus/p1_scenario.py",
)
EXPECTED_RUNNER_PINS = (
    "EXPECTED_SOURCE_COMMIT",
    "EXPECTED_BINARY_SHA256",
    "EXPECTED_REPOSITORY",
    "EXPECTED_INPUT_MANIFEST_SHA256",
)


class PreparationError(ValueError):
    """The requested package cannot be frozen from the supplied inputs."""


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    path = _regular_file(path, "file")
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def _regular_file(value: Path, label: str) -> Path:
    value = Path(value)
    try:
        info = value.lstat()
    except OSError as error:
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} is unavailable: {value}") from error
    if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode) or not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} must be a regular file: {value}")
    return value


def _directory(value: Path, label: str) -> Path:
    value = Path(value)
    try:
        info = value.lstat()
    except OSError as error:
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} is unavailable: {value}") from error
    if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode) or not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} must be a real directory: {value}")
    return value


def _json(path: Path, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        value = json.loads(_regular_file(path, label).read_text())
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
        raise PreparationError(f"cannot read {label}: {path}") from error
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} must be a JSON object: {path}")
    return value


def _hash_field(value: Any, label: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not HASH_RE.fullmatch(value):
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} must be a SHA-256")
    return value


def _require_hash(path: Path, expected: str, label: str) -> str:
    actual = sha256(path)
    if actual != expected:
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} hash mismatch")
    return actual


def _load_budget():
    path = TEMPLATE_ROOT / "collector" / "batch_budget.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("prepare_batch_budget", path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise PreparationError("cannot load batch budget controls")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def _runner_pins(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(_regular_file(path, "runner").read_text())
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, SyntaxError) as error:
        raise PreparationError(f"runner is not valid Python: {path}") from error
    pins: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for node in tree.body:
        if not isinstance(node, ast.Assign) or len(node.targets) != 1:
            continue
        target = node.targets[0]
        if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id in EXPECTED_RUNNER_PINS:
            try:
                pins[target.id] = ast.literal_eval(node.value)
            except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
                raise PreparationError(f"runner pin is not a literal: {target.id}") from error
    missing = [name for name in EXPECTED_RUNNER_PINS if name not in pins]
    if missing:
        raise PreparationError("runner pins missing: " + ", ".join(missing))
    return pins


def _validate_inputs(args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, Any]:
    source_root = _directory(args.source_root, "source root")
    source_archive = _regular_file(args.source_archive, "source archive")
    tracked_manifest = _regular_file(args.tracked_manifest, "tracked manifest")
    binary = _regular_file(args.binary, "evaluator binary")
    build_path = _regular_file(args.build_manifest, "build manifest")
    corpus_path = _regular_file(args.corpus_manifest, "corpus manifest")
    gate_path = _regular_file(args.full_check_gate, "full-check gate")
    runner = _regular_file(args.runner, "runner")
    source_commit = args.source_commit.lower()
    source_digest = args.source_digest.lower()
    if not COMMIT_RE.fullmatch(source_commit):
        raise PreparationError("source commit must be a 40-character lowercase Git identity")
    _hash_field(source_digest, "source digest")
    if not ID_RE.fullmatch(args.dispatch_id):
        raise PreparationError("dispatch ID must be a path-safe lowercase identifier")
    if not args.owner_id or any(char.isspace() for char in args.owner_id):
        raise PreparationError("owner ID must be a non-empty token without whitespace")
    build = _json(build_path, "build manifest")
    corpus = _json(corpus_path, "corpus manifest")
    gate = _json(gate_path, "full-check gate")
    binary_digest = sha256(binary)
    if build.get("source_commit") != source_commit or build.get("binary_sha256") != binary_digest:
        raise PreparationError("build manifest is not bound to source commit and binary")
    if type(build.get("exit_code")) is not int or build["exit_code"] != 0:
        raise PreparationError("build manifest does not record a successful build")
    source_archive_digest = sha256(source_archive)
    tracked_manifest_digest = sha256(tracked_manifest)
    if build.get("source_archive_sha256") != source_archive_digest:
        raise PreparationError("source archive hash does not match build manifest")
    if build.get("tracked_manifest_sha256") != tracked_manifest_digest:
        raise PreparationError("tracked manifest hash does not match build manifest")
    if type(build.get("tracked_file_count")) is not int or build["tracked_file_count"] <= 0:
        raise PreparationError("build manifest has no positive tracked file count")

    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument("--source-root", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--source-archive", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--tracked-manifest", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--binary", type=Path, required=True)

    p.add_argument("--write", dest="dry_run", action="store_false", help="write a new prepared package")
    p.set_defaults(dry_run=True)
    return p


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        print(json.dumps(prepare(args), sort_keys=True))
    except PreparationError as error:
        print(f"prepare failed: {error}")
        return 2

    except OSError as error:
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} is unavailable: {value}") from error
    if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode) or not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} must be a regular file: {value}")
    return value


def _directory(value: Path, label: str) -> Path:
    value = Path(value)
    try:
        info = value.lstat()
    except OSError as error:
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} is unavailable: {value}") from error
    if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode) or not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} must be a real directory: {value}")
    return value


def _json(path: Path, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        value = json.loads(_regular_file(path, label).read_text())
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
        raise PreparationError(f"cannot read {label}: {path}") from error
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} must be a JSON object: {path}")
    return value


def _hash_field(value: Any, label: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not HASH_RE.fullmatch(value):
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} must be a SHA-256")
    return value


def _require_hash(path: Path, expected: str, label: str) -> str:
    actual = sha256(path)
    if actual != expected:
        raise PreparationError(f"{label} hash mismatch")
    return actual


def _load_budget():
    path = TEMPLATE_ROOT / "collector" / "batch_budget.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("prepare_batch_budget", path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise PreparationError("cannot load batch budget controls")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def _runner_pins(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(_regular_file(path, "runner").read_text())
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, SyntaxError) as error:
        raise PreparationError(f"runner is not valid Python: {path}") from error
    pins: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for node in tree.body:
        if not isinstance(node, ast.Assign) or len(node.targets) != 1:
            continue
        target = node.targets[0]
        if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id in EXPECTED_RUNNER_PINS:
            try:
                pins[target.id] = ast.literal_eval(node.value)
            except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
                raise PreparationError(f"runner pin is not a literal: {target.id}") from error
    missing = [name for name in EXPECTED_RUNNER_PINS if name not in pins]
    if missing:
        raise PreparationError("runner pins missing: " + ", ".join(missing))
    return pins


def _validate_inputs(args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, Any]:
    source_root = _directory(args.source_root, "source root")
    source_archive = _regular_file(args.source_archive, "source archive")
    tracked_manifest = _regular_file(args.tracked_manifest, "tracked manifest")
    binary = _regular_file(args.binary, "evaluator binary")
    build_path = _regular_file(args.build_manifest, "build manifest")
    corpus_path = _regular_file(args.corpus_manifest, "corpus manifest")
    gate_path = _regular_file(args.full_check_gate, "full-check gate")
    runner = _regular_file(args.runner, "runner")
    source_commit = args.source_commit.lower()
    source_digest = args.source_digest.lower()
    if not COMMIT_RE.fullmatch(source_commit):
        raise PreparationError("source commit must be a 40-character lowercase Git identity")
    _hash_field(source_digest, "source digest")
    if not ID_RE.fullmatch(args.dispatch_id):
        raise PreparationError("dispatch ID must be a path-safe lowercase identifier")
    if not args.owner_id or any(char.isspace() for char in args.owner_id):
        raise PreparationError("owner ID must be a non-empty token without whitespace")
    build = _json(build_path, "build manifest")
    corpus = _json(corpus_path, "corpus manifest")
    gate = _json(gate_path, "full-check gate")
    binary_digest = sha256(binary)
    if build.get("source_commit") != source_commit or build.get("binary_sha256") != binary_digest:
        raise PreparationError("build manifest is not bound to source commit and binary")
    if type(build.get("exit_code")) is not int or build["exit_code"] != 0:
        raise PreparationError("build manifest does not record a successful build")
    source_archive_digest = sha256(source_archive)
    tracked_manifest_digest = sha256(tracked_manifest)
    if build.get("source_archive_sha256") != source_archive_digest:
        raise PreparationError("source archive hash does not match build manifest")
    if build.get("tracked_manifest_sha256") != tracked_manifest_digest:
        raise PreparationError("tracked manifest hash does not match build manifest")
    if type(build.get("tracked_file_count")) is not int or build["tracked_file_count"] <= 0:
        raise PreparationError("build manifest has no positive tracked file count")
    if corpus.get("manifest") != "p1-corpus-v1" or not isinstance(corpus.get("repositories"), list):
        raise PreparationError("unsupported corpus manifest")
    repositories = {item.get("id"): item for item in corpus["repositories"] if isinstance(item, dict)}
    repository = repositories.get(args.repository)
    if repository is None or not COMMIT_RE.fullmatch(str(repository.get("commit", ""))):
        raise PreparationError("selected repository is absent or has no frozen commit")
    repository_commit = repository["commit"]
    input_manifest_digest = sha256(corpus_path)
    if gate.get("schema") != "full-check-canonical-v1" or gate.get("status") != "passed":
        raise PreparationError("full-check gate is not a passed canonical gate")
    if gate.get("admission_eligible") is not False or gate.get("required_for_execution") is not True:
        raise PreparationError("full-check gate execution boundary changed")
    if gate.get("evaluator_source_commit") != source_commit or gate.get("evaluator_binary_sha256") != binary_digest:
        raise PreparationError("full-check gate is not bound to source and binary")
    if gate.get("evaluator_build_manifest_sha256") != sha256(build_path):
        raise PreparationError("full-check gate is not bound to build manifest")
    if gate.get("source_archive_sha256") != source_archive_digest or gate.get("tracked_manifest_sha256") != tracked_manifest_digest:
        raise PreparationError("full-check gate source capture binding changed")
    pins = _runner_pins(runner)
    expected_pins = {
        "EXPECTED_SOURCE_COMMIT": source_commit,
        "EXPECTED_BINARY_SHA256": binary_digest,
        "EXPECTED_REPOSITORY": args.repository,
        "EXPECTED_INPUT_MANIFEST_SHA256": input_manifest_digest,
    }
    for name, expected in expected_pins.items():
        if pins[name] != expected:
            raise PreparationError(f"runner pin mismatch: {name}")
    if args.unit != args.dispatch_id + ".service":
        raise PreparationError("unit must be dispatch ID plus .service")
    for label, value in (("remote source root", args.remote_source_root),
                         ("remote output root", args.remote_output_root),
                         ("remote claim path", args.remote_claim_path)):
        if not value.startswith("/") or ".." in Path(value).parts:
            raise PreparationError(f"{label} must be an absolute path without ..")
    if args.dispatch_id not in args.remote_output_root or args.dispatch_id not in args.remote_claim_path:
        raise PreparationError("remote paths must contain the dispatch ID")
    budget = _load_budget()
    cell = {
        "worker": 1,
        "repository": args.repository,
        "profile": "full",
        "verb": "snapshot",
        "scenario": "diagnostic",
        "trial": 0,
        "arms": [False],
        "preparatory_invocations": 0,
    }
    cell["cell_id"] = budget.cell_id(cell)
    batch = {
        "version": 1,
        "cap": CAP,
        "batch_id": args.dispatch_id,
        "scope": "bounded-diagnostic",
        "identity": {
            "binary_sha256": binary_digest,
            "input_manifest_sha256": input_manifest_digest,
            "runner_sha256": sha256(runner),
            "scenario_sha256": sha256(TEMPLATE_ROOT / "corpus" / "p1_scenario.py"),
            "gate_sha256": sha256(TEMPLATE_ROOT / "collector" / "campaign_gate.py"),
            "budget_sha256": sha256(TEMPLATE_ROOT / "collector" / "batch_budget.py"),
            "build_manifest_sha256": sha256(build_path),
        },
        "cells": [cell],
        "workers": {"1": 1},
    }
    batch = budget.validate(batch, batch["identity"])
    return {
        "source_root": source_root,
        "source_archive": source_archive,
        "tracked_manifest": tracked_manifest,
        "binary": binary,
        "build_path": build_path,
        "corpus_path": corpus_path,
        "gate_path": gate_path,
        "runner": runner,
        "build": build,
        "corpus": corpus,
        "gate": gate,
        "binary_digest": binary_digest,
        "source_archive_digest": source_archive_digest,
        "tracked_manifest_digest": tracked_manifest_digest,
        "input_manifest_digest": input_manifest_digest,
        "batch": batch,
        "cell_id": cell["cell_id"],
        "repository_commit": repository_commit,
    }


def _manifest(args: argparse.Namespace, values: dict[str, Any], build_digest: str,
              batch_digest: str, gate_digest: str, archive_digest: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    template = _json(TEMPLATE_ROOT / "controller" / "manifest.json", "manifest template")
    result = copy.deepcopy(template)
    result.update({
        "status": "prepared only; no VM, cloud, collector, product, corpus, or benchmark execution",
        "dispatch_id": args.dispatch_id,
        "source_commit": args.source_commit.lower(),
        "source_digest": args.source_digest.lower(),
        "source_archive_sha256": values["source_archive_digest"],
        "tracked_manifest_sha256": values["tracked_manifest_digest"],
        "binary_sha256": values["binary_digest"],
        "input_manifest_sha256": values["input_manifest_digest"],
        "build_manifest_sha256": build_digest,
        "batch_manifest_sha256": batch_digest,
        "full_check_gate_sha256": gate_digest,
        "control_archive_sha256": archive_digest,
        "cell_id": values["cell_id"],
        "repository": args.repository,
        "frozen_repository_commit": values["repository_commit"],
        "remote_source_root": args.remote_source_root,
        "remote_output_root": args.remote_output_root,
        "remote_claim_path": args.remote_claim_path,
        "product_deadline_seconds": None,
        "product_timeout_mode": "none-user-authorized-completion",
        "batch_manifest": "batch-manifest.json",
        "build_manifest": "build-manifest.json",
        "control_archive": "control-files.tar.gz",
        "full_check_gate": "full-check-gate.json",
        "controller_lease": {"owner_id": args.owner_id, "dispatch_id": args.dispatch_id, "unit": args.unit},
    })
    result["systemd_service"] = dict(result.get("systemd_service", {}), unit=args.unit)
    result["full_check"] = {
        "source_commit": values["gate"].get("evaluator_source_commit"),
        "evidence_commit": values["gate"].get("full_check_evidence_commit"),
        "status": values["gate"].get("status"),
        "statusline_failed": values["gate"].get("claims", {}).get("correctness") is False,
        "full_coverage_claimed": values["gate"].get("disclosed_limitations", {}).get("full_coverage_claimed"),
    }
    return result


def _write_json(path: Path, value: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")


def _archive(root: Path, destination: Path) -> str:
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=buffer, mode="w", format=tarfile.GNU_FORMAT) as archive:
        for name in CONTROL_MEMBERS:
            path = root / name
            info = archive.gettarinfo(str(path), arcname=name)
            info.uid = info.gid = 0
            info.uname = info.gname = ""
            info.mtime = 0
            with path.open("rb") as stream:
                archive.addfile(info, stream)
    import gzip
    with destination.open("wb") as stream:
        with gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=stream, mode="wb", mtime=0) as compressed:
            compressed.write(buffer.getvalue())
    return sha256(destination)


def prepare(args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, Any]:
    values = _validate_inputs(args)
    summary = {
        "status": "validated; no files written" if args.dry_run else "prepared",
        "dispatch_id": args.dispatch_id,
        "owner_id": args.owner_id,
        "source_commit": args.source_commit.lower(),
        "binary_sha256": values["binary_digest"],
        "input_manifest_sha256": values["input_manifest_digest"],
        "derived_invocations": values["batch"]["derived_invocations"],
        "output": str(args.output),
    }
    if args.dry_run:
        return summary
    output = Path(args.output)
    if output.exists():
        raise PreparationError(f"refusing to overwrite existing output: {output}")
    if not output.parent.is_dir():
        raise PreparationError(f"output parent must already exist: {output.parent}")
    temporary = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f".{output.name}.", dir=output.parent))
    try:
        for name in TEMPLATE_MEMBERS:
            destination = temporary / name
            destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            source = values["runner"] if name == "collector/run_remote.py" else TEMPLATE_ROOT / name
            shutil.copyfile(source, destination)
        shutil.copyfile(values["corpus_path"], temporary / "corpus/corpus-manifest.json")
        shutil.copyfile(values["build_path"], temporary / "build-manifest.json")
        shutil.copyfile(values["gate_path"], temporary / "full-check-gate.json")
        batch_path = temporary / "batch-manifest.json"
        _write_json(batch_path, values["batch"])
        hashes = "".join(f"{sha256(temporary / name)}  {name}\n" for name in CONTROL_MEMBERS if name != "control-hashes.txt")
        (temporary / "control-hashes.txt").write_text(hashes)
        archive_digest = _archive(temporary, temporary / "control-files.tar.gz")
        manifest = _manifest(args, values, sha256(temporary / "build-manifest.json"),
                            sha256(batch_path), sha256(temporary / "full-check-gate.json"), archive_digest)
        (temporary / "controller").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _write_json(temporary / "controller/manifest.json", manifest)
        os.replace(temporary, output)
    except BaseException:
        shutil.rmtree(temporary)
        raise
    summary["control_archive_sha256"] = archive_digest
    return summary


def parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument("--source-root", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--source-archive", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--tracked-manifest", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--binary", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--build-manifest", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--corpus-manifest", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--full-check-gate", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--runner", type=Path, default=TEMPLATE_ROOT / "collector/run_remote.py")
    p.add_argument("--source-commit", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--source-digest", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--repository", default="kubernetes-kubernetes")
    p.add_argument("--dispatch-id", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--owner-id", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--unit", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--remote-source-root", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--remote-output-root", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--remote-claim-path", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--write", dest="dry_run", action="store_false", help="write a new prepared package")
    p.set_defaults(dry_run=True)
    return p


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        print(json.dumps(prepare(args), sort_keys=True))
    except PreparationError as error:
        print(f"prepare failed: {error}")
        return 2
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

entire session adopt — Adopt an active session from another worktree
Adopt an active session from another worktree into the current repository.

This is useful when an agent starts in one repository or worktree, then moves
and makes changes in another. Adoption moves the live session state into the
current repo and seeds it with the current repo's uncommitted file changes so
the next commit can be linked normally.

When the source and target share a Git session store, adoption moves the same
session state file to the current worktree and requires --force or --yes.

Examples:
entire session adopt 019ed5fe-ec49-7a72-89fd-f38e323f5448 --from ../cli
  entire session adopt --from /path/to/source/worktree
  entire session adopt --from ../source-worktree --yes

Flags:
      --force         replace an existing local state file for the same session
      --from string   source worktree that already tracks the session

item.stdout:
entire session attach — Attach an existing agent session
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The

item.stdout:
entire checkpoint explain — Explain a session, commit, or checkpoint
Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo owner/name
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (positional or --checkpoint) and a
                 checkpoint that has been pushed.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied.
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript
                   while checkpoints v1 is the checkpoint store.
  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note
                   says how many were skipped. Only meaningful with --json.

Summary generation:
  --generate    Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
  --force       Regenerate even if a summary already exists (requires --generate)

Performance options:
  --search-all  Remove branch/depth limits when searching for commits (may be slow)

Checkpoint detail view shows:
  - Author of the checkpoint
  - Associated git commits that reference the checkpoint
  - Prompts and responses from the session

Note: --session filters the list view; the positional arg, --commit, and --checkpoint are mutually exclusive.

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-graph  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -c, --checkpoint string             Explain a specific checkpoint (ID or prefix)
      --commit string                 Explain a specific commit (SHA or ref, "commit-ish")
      --force                         Regenerate summary even if one already exists (requires --generate)
      --full                          Show full parsed transcript (all prompts/responses)
      --generate                      Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
      --insecure-http-auth            Allow plain-HTTP auth for --repo (local dev only)
      --json                          Output metadata as JSON (no transcript bytes)
      --limit int                     Cap the list view at N checkpoints (default: 100). Only meaningful with --json.
      --no-pager                      Disable pager output
      --raw-transcript                Show raw transcript file (JSONL format)
      --repo string                   Explain a checkpoint owned by another repo (owner/name or gh/owner/name), read from that repo's Entire API
      --search-all                    Search all commits (no branch/depth limit, may be slow)
      --session string                Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)
      --session-index int             Session index within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based, defaults to latest) (default -1)
  -s, --short                         Show summary only (omit prompts and files)
      --summary-timeout-seconds int   Hard deadline in seconds for --generate summary generation; overrides summary_timeout_seconds setting. 0 = use setting; if setting is also unset or 0, no automatic deadline applies.
      --transcript                    Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes to stdout

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Atomic remote-monotonic supervision lease for one completion diagnostic."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from contextlib import contextmanager
import fcntl
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import stat
import tempfile
import time


SCHEMA = "completion-supervisory-lease-v1"
LEASE_NAME = "supervisory-lease.json"
LOCK_NAME = "supervisory-lease.lock"
IDENTITY_NAME = "controller-lease.json"
BOOT_ID_PATH = Path("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id")
IDENTIFIER_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,95}$")
LEASE_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{32}$")
BOOT_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f-]{8,64}$")
TTL_SECONDS = 600
VALID_STATES = frozenset({"active", "expired", "released", "expired_cleanup_complete"})


class LeaseError(RuntimeError):
    """The exact supervisory lease cannot authorize continued product work."""


def _read_json(path: Path, label: str) -> dict:
    try:
        value = json.loads(path.read_text())
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
        raise LeaseError(f"cannot read {label}: {error}") from error
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise LeaseError(f"{label} is not a JSON object")
    return value


def _boot_id(path: Path = BOOT_ID_PATH) -> str:
    try:
        value = path.read_text().strip().lower()
    except OSError as error:
        raise LeaseError(f"cannot read remote boot identity: {error}") from error
    if not BOOT_ID_RE.fullmatch(value):
        raise LeaseError("remote boot identity is malformed")
    return value


def _identity(unit: str, dispatch_id: str, owner_id: str, lease_id: str) -> dict:
    if not IDENTIFIER_RE.fullmatch(dispatch_id) or not IDENTIFIER_RE.fullmatch(owner_id):
        raise LeaseError("supervisory lease identity is malformed")
    if not isinstance(unit, str) or unit != dispatch_id + ".service":
        raise LeaseError("supervisory lease unit does not match dispatch identity")
    if not LEASE_ID_RE.fullmatch(lease_id):
        raise LeaseError("supervisory lease ID is malformed")
    return {"owner_id": owner_id, "dispatch_id": dispatch_id, "unit": unit, "lease_id": lease_id}


def _verify_immutable_identity(remote_root: Path, identity: dict) -> None:
    expected = {key: identity[key] for key in ("owner_id", "dispatch_id", "unit")}
    if _read_json(remote_root / IDENTITY_NAME, "immutable controller identity") != expected:
        raise LeaseError("immutable controller identity mismatch")


def _validate_record(record: dict, identity: dict) -> dict:
    expected = {"schema": SCHEMA, **identity, "ttl_seconds": TTL_SECONDS}
    for key, value in expected.items():
        if record.get(key) != value:
            raise LeaseError(f"supervisory lease mismatch: {key}")
    if record.get("state") not in VALID_STATES:
        raise LeaseError("supervisory lease state is malformed")
    for key in ("generation", "issued_monotonic_ns", "renewed_monotonic_ns", "expires_monotonic_ns"):
        value = record.get(key)
        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
            raise LeaseError(f"supervisory lease field is malformed: {key}")
    if record["generation"] < 1:
        raise LeaseError("supervisory lease generation is malformed")
    boot_id = record.get("boot_id")
    if not isinstance(boot_id, str) or not BOOT_ID_RE.fullmatch(boot_id):
        raise LeaseError("supervisory lease boot identity is malformed")
    return record


def _atomic_write(path: Path, value: dict) -> None:
    descriptor, name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=path.name + ".", dir=path.parent)
    temporary = Path(name)
    try:
        os.fchmod(descriptor, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(descriptor, "w") as stream:
            json.dump(value, stream, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            stream.write("\n")
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        os.replace(temporary, path)
        directory = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
        try:
            os.fsync(directory)
        finally:
            os.close(directory)
    except BaseException:
        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise


@contextmanager
def _locked(remote_root: Path):
    remote_root = Path(remote_root)
    flags = os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR
    if hasattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW"):
        flags |= os.O_NOFOLLOW
    descriptor = os.open(remote_root / LOCK_NAME, flags, 0o600)
    try:
        info = os.fstat(descriptor)
        if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
            raise LeaseError("supervisory lease lock is not a regular file")
        fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        yield remote_root / LEASE_NAME
    finally:
        os.close(descriptor)


def initialize(remote_root, unit, dispatch_id, owner_id, lease_id, *,
               now_ns=None, boot_id=None) -> dict:
    """Create generation one once; an old package can never replay it."""
    remote_root = Path(remote_root)
    identity = _identity(unit, dispatch_id, owner_id, lease_id)
    _verify_immutable_identity(remote_root, identity)
    now = time.monotonic_ns() if now_ns is None else now_ns
    boot = _boot_id() if boot_id is None else boot_id
    if isinstance(now, bool) or not isinstance(now, int) or now < 0:
        raise LeaseError("remote monotonic time is malformed")
    if not isinstance(boot, str) or not BOOT_ID_RE.fullmatch(boot):
        raise LeaseError("remote boot identity is malformed")
    with _locked(remote_root) as path:
        if path.exists():
            raise LeaseError("supervisory lease already exists; refusing replay")
        record = {
            "schema": SCHEMA, **identity, "generation": 1, "state": "active",
            "boot_id": boot, "issued_monotonic_ns": now, "renewed_monotonic_ns": now,
            "expires_monotonic_ns": now + TTL_SECONDS * 1_000_000_000,
            "ttl_seconds": TTL_SECONDS,
        }
        _atomic_write(path, record)
        return record


def require_active(remote_root, unit, dispatch_id, owner_id, lease_id, *,
                   now_ns=None, boot_id=None) -> dict:
    """Validate liveness, durably expiring a same-identity stale lease."""
    remote_root = Path(remote_root)
    identity = _identity(unit, dispatch_id, owner_id, lease_id)
    _verify_immutable_identity(remote_root, identity)
    now = time.monotonic_ns() if now_ns is None else now_ns
    boot = _boot_id() if boot_id is None else boot_id
    with _locked(remote_root) as path:
        record = _validate_record(_read_json(path, "supervisory lease"), identity)
        loss = None
        if record["boot_id"] != boot:
            loss = "remote_boot_changed"
        elif record["state"] != "active":
            raise LeaseError(f"supervisory lease is not active: {record['state']}")
        elif now >= record["expires_monotonic_ns"]:
            loss = "supervisor_liveness_expired"
        if loss is not None:
            record["state"] = "expired"
            record["expired_monotonic_ns"] = now
            record["expiry_reason"] = loss
            _atomic_write(path, record)
            raise LeaseError(f"supervisory lease lost: {loss}")
        return record


def renew(remote_root, unit, dispatch_id, owner_id, lease_id, expected_generation, *,
          now_ns=None, boot_id=None) -> dict:
    """CAS-renew one still-active generation; expiry is irreversible."""
    remote_root = Path(remote_root)
    identity = _identity(unit, dispatch_id, owner_id, lease_id)
    _verify_immutable_identity(remote_root, identity)
    now = time.monotonic_ns() if now_ns is None else now_ns
    boot = _boot_id() if boot_id is None else boot_id
    if isinstance(expected_generation, bool) or not isinstance(expected_generation, int):
        raise LeaseError("expected supervisory lease generation is malformed")
    with _locked(remote_root) as path:
        record = _validate_record(_read_json(path, "supervisory lease"), identity)
        if record["state"] != "active":
            raise LeaseError(f"supervisory lease cannot renew from state: {record['state']}")
        if record["boot_id"] != boot or now >= record["expires_monotonic_ns"]:
            record["state"] = "expired"
            record["expired_monotonic_ns"] = now
            record["expiry_reason"] = (
                "remote_boot_changed" if record["boot_id"] != boot else "supervisor_liveness_expired"
            )
            _atomic_write(path, record)
            raise LeaseError("expired supervisory lease cannot be renewed")
        if record["generation"] != expected_generation:
            raise LeaseError("supervisory lease generation changed; recover exact state before renewal")
        record["generation"] += 1
        record["renewed_monotonic_ns"] = now
        record["expires_monotonic_ns"] = now + TTL_SECONDS * 1_000_000_000
        _atomic_write(path, record)
        return record


def recover(remote_root, unit, dispatch_id, owner_id, lease_id, *,
            now_ns=None, boot_id=None) -> dict:
    """Read exact remote state after ambiguity without extending or reviving it."""
    remote_root = Path(remote_root)
    identity = _identity(unit, dispatch_id, owner_id, lease_id)
    _verify_immutable_identity(remote_root, identity)
    now = time.monotonic_ns() if now_ns is None else now_ns
    boot = _boot_id() if boot_id is None else boot_id
    with _locked(remote_root) as path:
        record = _validate_record(_read_json(path, "supervisory lease"), identity)
        if record["boot_id"] != boot:
            raise LeaseError("supervisory lease belongs to an earlier remote boot")
        if record["state"] == "active" and now >= record["expires_monotonic_ns"]:
            raise LeaseError("expired supervisory lease cannot be recovered")
        return record


def complete(remote_root, unit, dispatch_id, owner_id, lease_id, outcome, *,
             now_ns=None, boot_id=None) -> dict:
    """Record cleanup only after the exact product unit has been stopped."""
    if outcome not in {"terminal", "cancelled", "expired"}:
        raise LeaseError("supervisory lease completion outcome is malformed")
    remote_root = Path(remote_root)
    identity = _identity(unit, dispatch_id, owner_id, lease_id)
    _verify_immutable_identity(remote_root, identity)
    now = time.monotonic_ns() if now_ns is None else now_ns
    boot = _boot_id() if boot_id is None else boot_id
    with _locked(remote_root) as path:
        record = _validate_record(_read_json(path, "supervisory lease"), identity)
        if record["boot_id"] != boot:
            raise LeaseError("supervisory lease belongs to an earlier remote boot")
        if record["state"] in {"released", "expired_cleanup_complete"}:
            if record.get("completion_outcome") != outcome:
                raise LeaseError("supervisory lease completion outcome changed")
            return record
        record["state"] = "expired_cleanup_complete" if record["state"] == "expired" else "released"
        record["completion_outcome"] = outcome
        record["completed_monotonic_ns"] = now
        _atomic_write(path, record)
        return record


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("action", choices=("initialize", "renew", "recover", "complete"))
    parser.add_argument("--remote-root", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--unit", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--dispatch-id", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--owner-id", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--lease-id", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-generation", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--outcome")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    positional = (args.remote_root, args.unit, args.dispatch_id, args.owner_id, args.lease_id)
    if args.action == "initialize":
        result = initialize(*positional)
    elif args.action == "renew":
        if args.expected_generation is None:
            parser.error("renew requires --expected-generation")
        result = renew(*positional, args.expected_generation)
    elif args.action == "recover":
        result = recover(*positional)
    else:
        if args.outcome is None:
            parser.error("complete requires --outcome")
        result = complete(*positional, args.outcome)
    print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bounded PID 1 smoke for the completion supervisor's lease and watchdog.

This deliberately launches only a local child that ignores TERM.  It must be
run as root on a disposable systemd host; it creates unique units and removes
them before returning.  It does not use a graph binary, corpus, claim, or
network endpoint.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import secrets
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time


COLLECTOR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "collector"
sys.path.insert(0, str(COLLECTOR))
import lease_remote
import run_remote


TTL_NS = lease_remote.TTL_SECONDS * 1_000_000_000
FAKE_CHILD = '''#!/usr/bin/python3
import os
import signal
import time
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(os.environ["SMOKE_ROOT"])
(root / "fake-child.pid").write_text(str(os.getpid()) + "\\n")
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN)
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
'''


def command(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(args, check=check, text=True, capture_output=True)


def show(unit: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    result = command("/usr/bin/systemctl", "show", unit,
                     "--property=ActiveState,SubState,Result,MainPID",
                     "--no-pager")
    values = {}
    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        values[key] = value
    return values


def wait_for(predicate, timeout: float, description: str):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        if predicate():
            return
        time.sleep(2)
    raise RuntimeError(f"timed out waiting for {description}")


def pid_alive(pid: int) -> bool:
    return pid > 0 and Path(f"/proc/{pid}").exists()


def identity(root: Path, dispatch: str, owner: str, lease_id: str) -> tuple:
    unit = dispatch + ".service"
    (root / lease_remote.IDENTITY_NAME).write_text(json.dumps({
        "owner_id": owner, "dispatch_id": dispatch, "unit": unit,
    }) + "\n")
    lease_remote.initialize(root, unit, dispatch, owner, lease_id)
    return unit, dispatch, owner, lease_id


def backdate_expiry(root: Path) -> None:
    """Expire only a synthetic smoke record while retaining the 600s span."""
    with lease_remote._locked(root) as path:
        record = json.loads(path.read_text())
        now = time.monotonic_ns()
        if now <= TTL_NS:
            raise RuntimeError("host monotonic uptime is shorter than the 600s lease span")
        expires = now - 1
        renewed = expires - TTL_NS
        record["issued_monotonic_ns"] = renewed
        record["renewed_monotonic_ns"] = renewed
        record["expires_monotonic_ns"] = expires
        lease_remote._atomic_write(path, record)


def start_service(script: Path, root: Path, unit: str, dispatch: str,
                  owner: str, lease_id: str) -> None:
    command(
        "/usr/bin/systemd-run", "--quiet", "--no-block", f"--unit={unit}",
        "--service-type=notify", "--property=NotifyAccess=main",
        "--property=TimeoutStartSec=30s", "--property=TimeoutStopSec=90s",
        "--property=WatchdogSec=90s", "--property=WatchdogSignal=SIGKILL",
        "--property=KillMode=control-group", "--property=Restart=no",
        "/usr/bin/python3", str(script), "--service", "--root", str(root),
        "--unit", unit, "--dispatch", dispatch, "--owner", owner,
        "--lease-id", lease_id,
    )
    wait_for(lambda: show(unit).get("ActiveState") == "active", 35,
             f"{unit} to become active")
    wait_for(lambda: (root / "fake-child.pid").is_file(), 10,
             f"{unit} fake child")


def stop_service(unit: str) -> None:
    command("/usr/bin/systemctl", "stop", unit, check=False)
    command("/usr/bin/systemctl", "reset-failed", unit, check=False)


def service(args) -> int:
    root = Path(args.root)
    lease_args = (root, args.unit, args.dispatch, args.owner, args.lease_id)
    notifier = run_remote.SystemdNotifier()
    notifier.ready()
    try:
        run_remote.run_process(
            root, root / "fake-child.py", os.environ.copy(),
            supervision_check=lambda: lease_remote.require_active(*lease_args),
            watchdog_heartbeat=notifier.heartbeat,
            poll_seconds=2,
            stop_grace_seconds=30,
        )
    except Exception as error:
        (root / "supervisor-result.json").write_text(json.dumps({
            "status": "issue", "error": str(error),
        }) + "\n")
        return 1
    return 0


def run_case(script: Path, root: Path, label: str) -> dict:
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    token = secrets.token_hex(8)
    dispatch = f"ga-smoke-{label}-{token}"
    owner = f"smoke-owner-{token}"
    lease_id = secrets.token_hex(16)
    unit, dispatch, owner, lease_id = identity(root, dispatch, owner, lease_id)
    start_service(script, root, unit, dispatch, owner, lease_id)
    child_pid = int((root / "fake-child.pid").read_text())
    if label == "renew":
        renewed = lease_remote.renew(*((root, unit, dispatch, owner, lease_id, 1)),
                                     boot_id=lease_remote._boot_id())
        if renewed["generation"] != 2 or not pid_alive(child_pid):
            raise RuntimeError("renewal did not preserve the owned child")
        if show(unit).get("ActiveState") != "active":
            raise RuntimeError("unit stopped after a valid lease renewal")
        stop_service(unit)
        lease_remote.complete(root, unit, dispatch, owner, lease_id, "cancelled")
        return {"case": label, "generation": renewed["generation"], "child_stopped": True}

    if label == "expiry":
        backdate_expiry(root)
        wait_for(lambda: show(unit).get("ActiveState") in {"failed", "inactive"}, 50,
                 "expired service cleanup")
        record = lease_remote.recover(root, unit, dispatch, owner, lease_id)
        result = json.loads((root / "supervisor-result.json").read_text())
        if record["state"] != "expired" or result["status"] != "issue":
            raise RuntimeError("expiry did not produce durable failure state")
        wait_for(lambda: not pid_alive(child_pid), 8, "expired child cleanup")
        stop_service(unit)
        return {"case": label, "lease_state": record["state"], "child_stopped": True}

    # Leave the main process frozen so PID 1, rather than Python cleanup code,
    # proves that the watchdog kills the whole control group.
    main_pid = int(show(unit).get("MainPID", "0"))
    if not pid_alive(main_pid):
        raise RuntimeError("systemd did not expose a live supervisor PID")
    time.sleep(3)
    os.kill(main_pid, signal.SIGSTOP)
    wait_for(lambda: show(unit).get("Result") == "watchdog", 110,
             "systemd watchdog failure")
    state = show(unit)
    if state.get("ActiveState") != "failed" or pid_alive(child_pid):
        raise RuntimeError(f"watchdog did not fail closed: {state}")
    stop_service(unit)
    return {"case": label, "result": state.get("Result"), "child_stopped": True}


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--service", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--unit")
    parser.add_argument("--dispatch")
    parser.add_argument("--owner")
    parser.add_argument("--lease-id")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.service:
        return service(args)
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        raise SystemExit("systemd supervision smoke must run as root")
    for binary in ("/usr/bin/systemd-run", "/usr/bin/systemctl"):
        if not os.access(binary, os.X_OK):
            raise SystemExit(f"required host binary is missing: {binary}")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="ga-supervision-smoke-") as temporary:
        root = Path(temporary)
        (root / "fake-child.py").write_text(FAKE_CHILD)
        (root / "fake-child.py").chmod(0o755)
        results = [run_case(Path(__file__).resolve(), root / label, label)
                   for label in ("renew", "expiry", "watchdog")]
        print(json.dumps({"cases": results, "evaluator_invoked": False}, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"` or a positive integer string.</multi_agent_role>
